extracted.intended_audience: general public (readers seeking information about GLAAD), journalists, media producers, LGBTQ+ advocates
extracted.subtask_description: Extracts and summarizes GLAAD's published/mentioned standards, indices, and guidance used to evaluate or improve media representation of LGBTQ people (style guide, indices, awards, and consultative practices).

rubrics_metrics.name: GLAAD Media Reference Guide (style guide)
rubrics_metrics.description: The GLAAD Media Reference Guide is a style guide of recommendations for writers, especially journalistic outlets, to reference in positive, inclusive depiction of LGBTQ people.
rubrics_metrics.guidance: Published since the 1990s (formerly the GLAAD Media Guide to the Lesbian and Gay Community); the 11th edition is cited (2022). Intended as prescriptive language/style guidance for journalists and writers to promote inclusive, positive depictions of LGBTQ people.

rubrics_metrics.name: Studio Responsibility Index (film representation index)
rubrics_metrics.description: Indexes "the quantity, quality and diversity of images of LGBTQ people in films released by six major motion picture studios."
rubrics_metrics.guidance: Launched August 2013 as an annual index; explicitly evaluates films on three dimensions: quantity, quality, and diversity of LGBTQ representation (applies to studio-released films).

rubrics_metrics.name: Social Media Safety Index (platform safety assessment)
rubrics_metrics.description: An index that assessed major social media platforms and concluded social media was "effectively unsafe for LGBTQ users."
rubrics_metrics.guidance: The 2021 Social Media Safety Index was based on analysis of Facebook, Instagram, TikTok, Twitter and YouTube. Used to evaluate platform-level safety for LGBTQ users (methodology details not provided on this page).

rubrics_metrics.name: Commentator Accountability Project (CAP)
rubrics_metrics.description: A project that "seeks to index and document frequent contributors, guests and pundits who regularly express anti-LGBTQ bias and misinformation in their contributions to journalism outlets."
rubrics_metrics.guidance: Launched March 2012; functions as an index/monitoring tool to identify and document media figures who consistently spread bias or misinformation, intended to hold commentators and outlets accountable.

rubrics_metrics.name: GLAAD Media Awards (recognition of media representation)
rubrics_metrics.description: Annual awards established in 1989 that recognize media for their representation of LGBTQ people; ceremonies are held in New York City, Los Angeles and San Francisco.
rubrics_metrics.guidance: The page does not list explicit award categories or scoring rules here, but the program functions as an evaluative recognition mechanism for media portrayals of LGBTQ people.

rubrics_metrics.name: Authentic and respectful representation practices (consultation & casting criteria)
rubrics_metrics.description: Guiding practice to ensure authentic portrayals of transgender and other LGBTQ characters via consultation and appropriate casting (e.g., ensuring a transgender protagonist is played by a trans actor; reviewing scripts to avoid offensive content).
rubrics_metrics.guidance: Illustrated by examples: GLAAD consulted on the game Tell Me Why and helped ensure Tyler would be played by a trans actor; GLAAD worked with Capcom on Street Fighter X Tekken 'to ensure that gaming’s most famous transgender character was portrayed with respect' and that 'anything that might be offensive has been very tailored to not be.' Also supported media figures preparing for interviews (e.g., Oprah and Elliot Page).

rubrics_metrics.name: Announcing Equality practice (inclusive announcement listings)
rubrics_metrics.description: An initiative resulting in more than 1,000 newspapers including gay and lesbian announcements alongside other wedding listings.
rubrics_metrics.guidance: Established in 2002; functions as a practical standard/expectation for newspapers to include same-sex wedding/announcement listings alongside other wedding announcements as a measure of equitable inclusion in print media.
